selection_status: 12 candidate topics selected after 204-record inventory was committed and read back
semantic_uniqueness_rule: Compare mechanism, workflow/transaction, failure class, evidence, remediation, question and topology fingerprints, not URL or title alone. Reject any candidate materially equivalent to a published or candidate-only record in the 30-day inventory.

topics.lesson_subject: Transparent conditional DNS forwarding: zone-matched interception, local answers, and site-local resolver selection
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: DNS proxy parses configured dns-database zones, matches QNAME/domain filters, checks local dns-entry data, then selects zone-specific forwarder or original destination; the database is attached to a DNS filter profile and only works on proxy-based firewall policies.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client sends DNS to its configured resolver; FortiGate transparently intercepts the query in a proxy inspection policy; matching zone chooses local answer or forwarder; unmatched names continue to original destination; response returns to client.
topics.failure_class: Wrong authoritative flag, unmatched zone, missing DNS-filter policy binding, flow-mode policy, unreachable forwarder, wrong source IP across VPN, or unsupported low-memory model.
topics.evidence_pattern: nslookup returns configured local A record for office.microsoft.com, local resolver answer for another matching name, and central resolver answer for unmatched facebook.com; packet capture shows client-to-FortiGate and FortiGate-to-forwarder transactions.
topics.remediation_path: Enable DNS Database feature visibility; define zone and local entries; disable authoritative when upstream fallback is intended; set forwarder and source-ip/source-ip6; attach zone to DNS filter profile; apply it to proxy-based policy; verify route, source address, and RAM/model support.
topics.question_fingerprint: Given local SaaS DNS answers differ from central answers, identify the domain-match decision and distinguish local-record, zone-forwarder, and unmatched-query paths.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Three-branch DNS decision graph: client query into FortiGate DNS proxy, QNAME match diamond, then local answer, zone forwarder, or original resolver; responses converge to client.

topics.lesson_subject: Per-policy workspace locking: granular concurrent-edit isolation and policy-sequence ownership
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Workspace mode plus per-policy-lock lets an administrator lock a single policy rather than an entire package or ADOM; policies used by Policy Blocks cannot be individually locked; adding/reordering multiple policies creates a separate sequence lock.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Administrator selects ADOM and package, acquires policy lock, edits and saves; competing administrators see lock owner/color and cannot modify that policy; sequence lock serializes insert/reorder operations and disappears after save.
topics.failure_class: Workspace/per-policy locking disabled, policy belongs to a Policy Block, stale lock ownership, or sequence lock blocks policy insertion/reordering.
topics.evidence_pattern: Green padlock identifies the current administrator's lock; red padlock identifies another administrator's lock; hover tooltip exposes owner and timestamp; sequence-lock banner appears when multiple policies are added.
topics.remediation_path: Enable Workspace mode and Per-Policy Lock in System Settings > Advanced > Workspace or set config system global per-policy-lock enable; verify correct ADOM/package; use package/ADOM lock for Policy Block members; complete save and release lock before handoff.
topics.question_fingerprint: Distinguish a single-policy edit lock from the sequence lock required for ordering changes and from whole-package/ADOM locks.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two-admin concurrency swimlane around one shared policy package, with single-policy lock and separate sequence-lock gate on insert/reorder.

topics.lesson_subject: Cloud archive offload with Storage Fabric Connectors: connector identity, CA trust, license gate, and remote-path binding
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer Device Log Settings binds an enabled Fabric storage connector and remote bucket/container path to log upload; a valid Storage Connector Service license and cloud-provider CA chain are prerequisites for S3, Azure Blob, or Google storage.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Create provider connector with region and credential material; import provider CA certificates; enable Upload logs to cloud storage; choose connector and remote path; FortiAnalyzer uploads log files to the configured cloud bucket/container.
topics.failure_class: Missing storage-service entitlement, disabled connector, incorrect provider region or credentials, wrong bucket/container path, missing CA chain, or outbound TLS/network failure.
topics.evidence_pattern: License Information shows entitlement; Fabric Connectors shows connector enabled; Device Log Settings shows selected connector and remote path; provider-side object listing/audit logs confirm upload; local Analytics and Archive availability must be checked separately.
topics.remediation_path: Validate Storage Connector Service license; create the correct S3/Azure Blob/Google connector; verify region and credential scope; import provider CA certificates; enable upload and set exact remote path; test outbound DNS/TLS and confirm provider-side objects.
topics.question_fingerprint: Identify which dependency explains a cloud upload failure when local log ingestion continues: connector entitlement, remote path, or CA trust.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer archive pipeline branching from local log storage through a license/connector/CA gate to cloud object storage, with analytics database shown as a separate local path.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiLink-managed dual-signed FortiSwitchOS image verification: controller validation and pre-upgrade trust evidence
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 7.6.5 switch controller adds OS image signature verification for dual-signed FortiSwitchOS images; FortiSwitchOS GUI also exposes image integrity verification, with model/BIOS support determining whether verification is available.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Administrator selects an image for a managed switch; controller and switch firmware-support path validate image signature/integrity before installation; unsupported BIOS or failed signature produces explicit warning rather than a clean verified state.
topics.failure_class: Unverified or invalid image signature, BIOS without signature-verification support, unsupported model/image combination, or assuming a successful file transfer equals trusted firmware.
topics.evidence_pattern: GUI warning 'Firmware failed signature validation', 'Unverified Image Detected', or red warning triangle; release/model feature matrix establishes whether BIOS and hardware support verification.
topics.remediation_path: Use an official Fortinet image for the exact model and supported release; verify model/feature matrix and BIOS capability; stop on signature warnings; remediate firmware/BIOS compatibility through supported upgrade guidance rather than bypassing verification.
topics.question_fingerprint: Differentiate image upload success from signature validation and identify the correct response to a BIOS-capability warning.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiManager/FortiGate controller to FortiLink switch upgrade flow with image intake, signature-verification gate, BIOS capability check, and install/stop branches.

topics.lesson_subject: Wi-Fi 7 Multi-Link Operation: MLD link association, WPA3 prerequisites, radio-profile binding, and standalone behavior
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAP-K MLO exposes one multi-link device across supported 2.4/5/6-GHz radios; requires FAP 7.6.3+, supported model/radio, WPA3-SAE with H2E-only or WPA3 Enterprise Only; standalone mode on supported K models requires FAP 7.6.5+, bridge mode and local authentication.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Create VAP with supported security and mlo enable; optionally set local-standalone/local-bridging/local-authentication; attach VAP to WTP profile radios; client negotiates MLD links; controller diagnostic reports link count and link IDs.
topics.failure_class: Unsupported AP/radio/firmware, incompatible WPA security or SAE H2E setting, VAP not applied to target radios, missing standalone bridge/local-auth prerequisites, or assuming association implies multi-link operation.
topics.evidence_pattern: diagnose wpa wpad mld displays num_links and link_id values; FortiAP vcfg output shows mlo; supported-model matrix distinguishes radios that cannot participate.
topics.remediation_path: Confirm K-series model and per-radio capability; upgrade AP firmware to supported version; configure WPA3/H2E and MLO; bind VAP to each intended radio in WTP profile; for standalone add local-standalone, local-bridging, and local-authentication; verify MLD link count.
topics.question_fingerprint: Interpret an MLD diagnostic with one active link versus three links and isolate model/radio/security/profile prerequisites.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: One Wi-Fi 7 MLD client connected to a single logical SSID across three radio links, with controller/WTP profile mapping and standalone-authentication branch.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiNAC 9.4 API/HTTPS SMS Gateway: connector-driven notifications and sponsor LDAP group mapping
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC 9.4 adds API/HTTPS SMS gateway integration alongside legacy Mail-to-SMS, including cloud-provider integration such as Twilio and LDAP group mapping for sponsors; notifications can target administrators, guests, and users.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiNAC event or user workflow selects a notification recipient; Email/SMS service connector routes the message through configured HTTPS provider integration; provider accepts request and delivers through its SMS network; sponsor eligibility is derived from configured LDAP group mapping.
topics.failure_class: Connector disabled or misconfigured, provider authentication/endpoint issue, outbound HTTPS/DNS failure, recipient normalization or provider quota failure, or sponsor group mapping not matching the intended LDAP group.
topics.evidence_pattern: FortiNAC Email/SMS connector configuration and event/notification records show message dispatch; provider-side request logs distinguish API acceptance from carrier delivery; sponsor group mapping can be compared with LDAP membership.
topics.remediation_path: Configure the 9.4 Email/SMS connector using the provider-supported settings; validate outbound DNS/TLS and provider credentials; test with a controlled recipient; verify provider acceptance and delivery separately; confirm sponsor LDAP group mapping and membership.
topics.question_fingerprint: Separate FortiNAC notification generation, HTTPS provider acceptance, carrier delivery, and LDAP sponsor authorization.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC event/guest workflow and LDAP sponsor group feed a recipient/connector decision, then HTTPS SMS provider and carrier delivery with acknowledgment boundary.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiLink integration credential planes: REST API token, SSH/CLI, SNMPv3, and separate RADIUS enforcement
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F 7.6.5+ uses a FortiGate REST API token in addition to—not instead of—System Administrator SSH/CLI and SNMPv3 for FortiLink-managed FortiSwitch/FortiAP inventory, L2/L3 polling and VLAN control; RADIUS remains the endpoint-authentication/dynamic-VLAN plane. Current FortiOS releases have version-specific token transport requirements.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F polls FortiGate REST API with token for managed inventory/MAC/VLAN state; SSH/CLI supplies FortiSwitch discovery and command functions; SNMPv3 supplies monitoring/traps; RADIUS handles endpoint authentication and CoA; token URL-parameter compatibility differs by FortiOS release and the legacy rest-api-key-url-query command is removed in FortiOS 8.0.
topics.failure_class: REST token missing/invalid or incompatible with FortiOS token transport, CLI credential removed so switches are not discovered, SNMPv3 removed so monitoring/traps disappear, or RADIUS mistakenly expected to be replaced by API credentials.
topics.evidence_pattern: FortiNAC FortiGate Model Configuration shows API token plus CLI/SNMP settings; Network Inventory shows FortiSwitch/FortiAP models; output.master shows REST API status and polling errors; community scenario notes token clearing after VLAN change when legacy query-parameter setting is absent.
topics.remediation_path: Create dedicated REST API Admin with minimum read or read/write scope and trusted host; add token to FortiGate model; retain CLI and SNMPv3; keep RADIUS separately; validate FortiOS/FortiNAC compatibility and do not apply the legacy rest-api-key-url-query workaround to FortiOS 8.0 where the command is removed.
topics.question_fingerprint: Given missing switch discovery, failed VLAN changes, or absent SNMP traps, map each symptom to the correct independent credential/protocol plane.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F connected to FortiGate/FortiLink with three parallel REST API, SSH/CLI and SNMPv3 management channels plus a separate endpoint-to-RADIUS authentication path.

topics.lesson_subject: SCEP with Microsoft Intune and Entra ID-backed EAP-TLS: OAuth challenge generation, certificate binding, and SAML group-to-RADIUS policy
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator 8.0 adds an Intune option for SCEP challenge-password generation using an Azure Directory OAuth server; remote SAML users can carry certificate bindings, SAML user groups can carry RADIUS attributes, and SAML realms/remote group filters can participate in RADIUS policy selection.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Intune requests SCEP enrollment; FortiAuthenticator uses Azure Directory OAuth/tenant ID to generate challenge password and issues certificate from local CA; EAP-TLS presents client certificate; remote SAML user certificate binding resolves identity; SAML group filter and RADIUS attributes supply authorization in the selected realm/policy.
topics.failure_class: SCEP disabled or HTTP interface access missing, invalid/expired CA, OAuth server lacks Azure tenant ID, unsupported Azure Government tenant, certificate binding mismatch, SAML group filter absent from RADIUS realm/policy, or missing RADIUS attributes.
topics.evidence_pattern: SCEP Enrollment Requests shows Pending/Approved/Rejected and issuer/subject; certificate chain and SAN/UPN binding identify the enrolled endpoint/user; RADIUS session and policy logs show realm, matched group and returned attributes.
topics.remediation_path: Enable SCEP and HTTP on serving interface; validate local CA; configure Azure Directory OAuth with tenant ID; choose InTune challenge-password generation; configure remote SAML user certificate bindings and group RADIUS attributes; add SAML realm/group filter to RADIUS policy; test enrollment and EAP-TLS separately.
topics.question_fingerprint: Trace a certificate from Intune SCEP issuance through remote SAML identity binding into RADIUS group authorization without confusing enrollment with authentication.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Intune SCEP enrollment/OAuth/CA issuance path converges with EAP-TLS certificate presentation, SAML user/group binding and RADIUS policy attribute response.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiPAM 1.9 agentless web launchers: browser tab-sharing consent, recording upload, and launcher limitations
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Agentless mode launches supported web-based secrets without FortiClient or the Privileged Access Agent browser extension; automatic mode prioritizes FortiClient, then extension, then agentless; Web Browsing is excluded, Firefox unsupported, and macOS requires screen/audio recording permission.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User launches supported web secret; browser asks permission to share FortiPAM tab; session header shows lifetime and Stop sharing; stopping sharing or closing tab terminates session and uploads video; native launchers are unaffected by the agentless selector.
topics.failure_class: Unsupported browser or launcher, tab-sharing consent not granted, macOS screen/system-audio permission missing, Web RDP resolution expectation, or assuming agentless mode supports native/Web Browsing launchers.
topics.evidence_pattern: Banner shows selected Agentless mode; browser tab displays Allow prompt and Stop sharing header; session lifetime is visible; video appears in logs after Stop sharing; browser warning appears when extension absent.
topics.remediation_path: Use Chrome or Edge and a supported web launcher; select Agentless explicitly or verify automatic priority; grant tab sharing; on macOS grant Screen & System Audio Recording; use Stop sharing to close and upload recording; use supported mode for Web Browsing/native launchers.
topics.question_fingerprint: Determine why a Web SSH/RDP session opens but its recording is missing, and distinguish agentless launcher support from Web Browsing/native launchers.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM mode selector to Chrome/Edge tab-sharing permission, proxied web launcher session and recording-upload branch; unsupported launcher/browser exits.

topics.lesson_subject: AWS Security Hub integration: regional findings ingestion, SDK credential scope, and FortiSIEM discovery
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM 7.5.1 integrates AWS Security Hub through the AWS Security Hub SDK/PHP V3 SDK; Security Hub findings are region-scoped and FortiSIEM credentials can specify multiple AWS region codes for discovery and ingestion.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Enable Security Hub in each intended AWS region; create IAM access key with documented permissions; create FortiSIEM credential using Device Type Amazon AWS Security Hub and Access Protocol AWS Security Hub SDK with region list; test connectivity; run AWS Scan discovery; ingest findings as FortiSIEM events.
topics.failure_class: Security Hub disabled in one or more regions, wrong region code, insufficient IAM permissions, invalid access key, incorrect credential-to-region association, or assuming one region's findings cover all accounts/regions.
topics.evidence_pattern: FortiSIEM credential shows AWS Security Hub SDK and region list; Test Connectivity succeeds; CMDB discovery records AWS Security Hub; Resources > Event Types contains AWS Sechub types and incoming finding events.
topics.remediation_path: Enable Security Hub in every intended region; validate IAM permissions against Fortinet's documented integration requirements and least privilege; use correct region codes in credential; test connectivity; rerun AWS Scan; confirm findings exist in each region before troubleshooting FortiSIEM parsing.
topics.question_fingerprint: Explain why a working Security Hub integration reports findings from one region but not another and identify the regional enablement boundary.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Multiple AWS regions each with Security Hub findings feed a single FortiSIEM AWS SDK credential/discovery path, then CMDB and event/rule/report pipeline.

topics.lesson_subject: Inline-CASB application detection and SaaS tenant restriction: deep inspection, HTTP header insertion, and per-application overrides
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Inline-CASB uses IPS protocol decoders to detect SaaS application traffic on HTTP/1.0, 1.1 and 2.0, including non-standard ports; SSL deep inspection exposes HTTPS payloads for application-control decisions and Web Filter Inline-CASB can insert/remove tenant-restriction HTTP headers.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Endpoint traffic enters FortiSASE policy; deep inspection terminates/re-establishes TLS using trusted FortiSASE CA; application decoder identifies SaaS; category action allow/monitor/block is evaluated with per-app override; optional Web Filter header rule modifies matching HTTP request; vendor enforces tenant identifier.
topics.failure_class: Certificate inspection used instead of deep inspection, endpoint does not trust FortiSASE CA, profile group not attached to matching policy, unsupported QUIC/HTTP version, malformed tenant ID/header, or traffic bypasses FortiSASE.
topics.evidence_pattern: Web Filter with Inline-CASB logs show application match and inserted header under Change Headers/Details; FortiView Cloud Applications shows access attempts; corporate tenant works while disallowed account is rejected by SaaS vendor.
topics.remediation_path: Enable SSL deep inspection and deploy trusted CA; enable Inline-CASB application control and Web Filter in the same security profile group; attach profile to matching policy; define FQDN destination group and exact vendor header; block QUIC where required; validate UUID and ensure traffic traverses FortiSASE.
topics.question_fingerprint: Differentiate application-category blocking from tenant-restriction header insertion and diagnose why certificate inspection cannot expose the required HTTP header.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Remote endpoint through FortiSASE TLS inspection and IPS application decoder, category/override policy, optional HTTP header insertion, SaaS tenant decision and logs.

topics.lesson_subject: SD-WAN Setup Wizard: license-gated generation of zone, members, SLA and service rule with a separate default-route step
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 8.0 SD-WAN Setup Wizard creates a zone, up to two member interfaces, gateway/cost/fallback priority, Performance SLA and SD-WAN service rule; it requires valid SD-WAN Underlay and Application Monitoring licenses and does not create the required default static route automatically.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Wizard gathers underlay interfaces and gateway/priority; creates or selects zone and members; selects FortiGuard or manual SLA; creates service rule or uses implicit rule; review applies generated objects; administrator separately adds static route to SD-WAN zone.
topics.failure_class: Missing license hides wizard, more than two underlays exceeds wizard scope, wrong cost/fallback priority affects path selection, SLA target unsuitable, or omitted default static route leaves traffic on another route.
topics.evidence_pattern: Network > SD-WAN shows created zone/members/health-check/rule; Network > Static Routes must separately show default route to SD-WAN zone; SLA status and session route confirm actual steering.
topics.remediation_path: Confirm both required licenses; use wizard only for two-underlay bootstrap; inspect generated members, gateway, cost, priority, SLA target and service strategy; add the default static route manually; verify firewall policy and route selection before testing application steering.
topics.question_fingerprint: Identify why a completed wizard creates SD-WAN objects but traffic still follows the old default route, and distinguish SLA state from route installation.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Wizard stages from licensed underlay selection through zone/member creation, SLA, service rule and review, followed by a separate static-route/policy gate to traffic forwarding.
